usage: novamind-operation [-h]
                          {new-session,next-week,python,python-c,query,status,history,list-sessions,stop} ...

CEOBench Simulation CLI

positional arguments:
  {new-session,next-week,python,python-c,query,status,history,list-sessions,stop}
    new-session         Create a new simulation session
    next-week           Advance simulation by one week (7 days). Requires a
                        rationale string + 12 cash forecasts.
    python              Execute a Python script with novamind_api
    python-c            Execute inline Python code with novamind_api
    query               Execute a SQL query
    status              Get session status
    history             View action history
    list-sessions       List all sessions
    stop                Stop the simulation server

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

  ./novamind-operation new-session --days 365 --seed 42

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 1, Day 7)
- Cash: ~$371k (after initial R&D and Research spend)
- Subscribers: 0
- Quality: Low (~0.12 - 0.18)
- Leads: 140/week (all lost due to low quality)

## Actions Taken
- Started R&D Tier 1 and 2 ($500k). Completion expected Day 19-24.
- Increased Global Dev spend to $2000/day.
- Targeted Dev spend for S1: $8000/day to boost quality rapidly (+0.21/week).
- Upgraded Model Tiers: Plan A=2, B=3, C=4.
- Set targeted ads for S1 ($400/day) and S3 ($200/day).
- Discovered "Real Estate Groups" (E).
- Researching S1 to Level 2 to reduce noise.

## Hypotheses
- High targeted dev spend on S1 will make our product irresistible to them within 1-2 weeks.
- Tier 2 for Plan A provides a better quality/price ratio for S1 without significantly increasing compute costs.
- S1 will be our initial "engine" for cash flow.

## To Watch
- Subscriber growth in S1 starting Day 10-14.
- Cash burn: ~$11k/day is sustainable for ~4-5 weeks. Must see revenue or cut spend by then.
- R&D completion and quality boost.

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 3, Day 21)
- Cash: $79,859 (CRITICAL).
- Subscribers: 82 (81 S1, 1 S2).
- Burn: Reduced from $10k/day to ~$1.1k/day.
- Quality: S1 (0.33), S2 (0.23), S3 (0.18).

## Actions Taken (Emergency Pivot)
- Slashed all targeted dev and targeted ad spending.
- Reduced Global Dev to $300/day and Global Ops to $200/day.
- Raised Price A to $25 (S1 WTP is $35).
- Increased Plan A Quota to 100/day to address user complaints.
- Kept Plan A on Model Tier 2 to maintain high quality (0.33) during price transition.

## Hypotheses
- S1 will accept $25/mo because quality is high (0.33) and usage caps were lifted.
- The reduced burn ($1.1k/day) buys ~10 weeks of runway, enough for R&D T1 and T2 to complete.
- Once R&D T1/T2 complete, S3 and S2 will become viable targets.

## To Watch
- R&D completion dates for T1 and T2.
- S1 churn rate at $25.
- Reputation impact of the support backlog (Ops cut might hurt this, but cash is priority).
- S3 conversion: Check if new S3 leads start subscribing to Plan C ($149) or B ($49) now that quality is 0.18.

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 7, Day 49)
- Cash: $26,237.
- Subscribers: 154 (103 Plan A, 51 Plan B).
- High number of downgrades (31) as S1 customers move from Plan B ($59) to Plan A ($29) to match their WTP (~$35).
- Burn: Net burn was ~$1.3k/day.
- Critical issue: Support backlog. Social sentiment is negative regarding support response times.
- Macro: PMI at 46.1 indicates economic contraction, tightening SaaS budgets.

## Actions Taken
- Drastically cut spending to preserve runway:
    - Ops: $500 -> $150.
    - Dev: $500 -> $100.
    - Capacity: Tier 1 ($215) -> Tier 0 ($85). (Usage ~12k/day fits well within Tier 0's 50k limit).
    - Ads: Cut LinkedIn and S3. Kept Social S1 ($30) and Search S2 ($30).
- Expected Burn: ~$250/day (down from $1,300).
- Expected Runway: ~100 days (14 weeks).
- Replied to a viral support complaint.

## Hypotheses
- Tier 0 capacity will handle current load with no performance impact.
- Cutting Ops to $150/day will still allow issue resolution (albeit slower) while staying sustainable.
- S1 customers will continue to consolidate on Plan A.
- S2 leads will continue to convert at Plan B or Plan A.

## To Watch
- Support sentiment: If complaints increase, may need to rethink Ops efficiency.
- Growth rate: Can we hit break-even before cash runs out? (Need ~550 subs).
- Competitor events: Macro environment is tough.
- Enterprise: Still unreachable until quality hits > 0.7.

## Current State (Week 9, Day 63)
- Cash: $21,184.
- Subscribers: 193 (Mostly S1).
- Growth: ~23 subs/week.
- Burn: Net burn is ~$4,700/week (high due to infrastructure upgrade and aggressive ads).
- Support: 12 open issues. Ops spend increased to $350/day.
- Infrastructure: Upgraded to Tier 1 (200k units) as usage hit 97k (Tier 0 limit 50k). This should fix "inconsistent quality" complaints.
- Quality: Plan A is below S2 floor. Started targeted Dev spend ($50/day) on S2 to raise their quality floor bonus.
- Discovery: Focusing on S3 (High margin) and D_E09 (Real Estate Enterprise).

## Actions Taken
- Capacity Tier 1 ($215/day).
- Ops Spend: $350/day (Backlog priority).
- Dev Spend: $150 global + $50 targeted S2.
- Ad Spend: $120/day total (E1 $20, D_E09 $20, S3 $40, S2 $20, S1 $20).
- Total Daily Spend: ~$925.

## Hypotheses
- Tier 1 infrastructure will restore quality consistency and stop "quality drop" complaints.
- $350/day Ops will clear the 12 issues within 1 week.
- Search ads for S3 will bring in high-value ($149) subscribers.
- Targeted Dev for S2 will make Plan A acceptable for them in a few weeks.

## To Watch
- Cash: Runway is down to ~4.4 weeks. MUST see growth in S2/S3 or Enterprise leads soon.
- S1 churn: If quality issues persist, S1 might leave.
- Enterprise: If LinkedIn doesn't yield leads in 2 weeks, pivot channel.

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 10, Day 70)
- Cash: $16,308.
- Subscribers: 209.
- Growth: 18 new subs, but 11 downgrades and 2 cancels.
- Burn: Net burn is ~$5,000/week.
- Support: 19 open issues. Sentiment is negative due to response times.
- Rivals: ApexSaaS, NexGen, and RivalTech launched updates (+0.10 quality boost to expectations).
- Macro: PMI is low (45-49), customers are cost-cutting.

## Actions Taken
- Upgraded Plan A to Tier 3 model (Sonnet/GPT-4o) to boost quality from 0.75x to 0.90x. This should put Plan A quality (~0.39) above the S2 floor (0.343) and counter rival updates.
- Increased Ops Spend to $450/day + $50 targeted S1 to clear the backlog.
- Targeted Ad Spend: Focus on S2, S3, E1, and D_E09.
- Lead Promotion: $5.00 off to help conversion during economic dip.
- Social Media: Addressing support and quality concerns.

## Hypotheses
- Tier 3 model for Plan A will stabilize S2 and S3 churn and attract more "quality-focused" individuals who are currently on the fence.
- Clearing the support backlog will stop the negative social media spiral.
- LinkedIn spend on D_E09 (Real Estate) is the best bet for a "save the company" enterprise hit.

## To Watch
- Cash: Runway is critical (3-4 weeks). If revenue doesn't jump, I'll have to cut all Dev/Ads.
- Downgrades: See if T3 model stops the slide from Plan B to A.
- Enterprise: Check LinkedIn leads daily.

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 11, Day 77)
- Cash: $10,536 (CRITICAL).
- Subscribers: 220 (Growth slowed).
- Burn: Reduced burn from ~$5,800/week to ~$1,350/week.
- Revenue: ~$1,700 - $2,100/week.
- **Status: REACHED BREAK-EVEN (SURVIVAL MODE).**
- Issues: 20 (Resolving at $100/day).
- Macro: Economic contraction (PMI 45-49).

## Actions Taken
- **Slashed Costs**: Dropped Capacity to Tier 0, Dev to $0, Ads to $0.
- **Model Efficiency**: Plan A downgraded to Tier 1, Plan B to Tier 2. S1 users (majority) are still well above quality floor.
- **Revenue**: Kept prices at $29/$59. Added 0.1 global ads strength for minor revenue boost.
- **Social**: Posted update about infrastructure optimization and support clearing.

## Hypotheses
- S1 users will not churn despite the quality drop to T1 model, as their floor is very low (0.088).
- $100/day Ops is sufficient to clear the 20-issue backlog and maintain stability.
- Staying alive during the economic contraction is the priority over growth.

## To Watch
- Churn: Monitor if S1 users react to the T1 model.
- Cash: Should see slight growth next week.
- Enterprise: Currently 0 leads/effort. Need to wait for cash reserves to build before restarting LinkedIn ads.

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 17, Day 119)
- Cash: $1,820 (CRITICAL).
- Subscribers: 220.
- Issues: 30 (Up from 22).
- **Status: SURVIVAL MODE.**
- Removed all lead promotions (was $20 for S1, killing margins).
- Stopped all advertising and development spending.
- Reduced Compute costs by dropping Plan B to Model Tier 2.
- Increased prices: A=$24, B=$54.

## Actions Taken
- `pricing.set_prices(A=24, B=54, C=129)`
- `pricing.set_model_tiers(A=1, B=2, C=3)`
- `marketing.set_daily_spend(operations=150, development=0)`
- `marketing.set_targeted_ad_spend(targeted_spend={})`
- `marketing.set_lead_promotion(global_promotion=0)`
- `marketing.set_ads_strength(global_strength=0.15)`

## Hypotheses
- By cutting Ads/Dev and lowering Model Tiers, we reduce burn to ~$250/day.
- Removing the $20 lead promotion on Plan A ($19 list) will turn new signups from a loss into a profit immediately.
- Increasing prices to $24/$54 will reach cash-flow positivity in ~4 weeks.
- Satisfaction should remain acceptable as delivered quality (0.42+) is still above S1 floors (0.09).

## To Watch
- Cash: Must not hit $0.
- Churn: Will the Tier 2 quality drop or Price increase trigger cancellations?
- Issues: Monitor if $150/day Ops clears the backlog.

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 19, Day 133)
- Cash: $580 (CRITICAL).
- Subscribers: 183 (Down from 214).
- Issues: 20 (Down from 23).
- **Status: SURVIVAL MODE (Approaching Break-even but high churn).**
- Net cash flow: ~$45/day burn last week.
- Major problem: Churn (31 last week) and poor customer support sentiment.
- Economy: PMI at 45.3 (Contraction). Customers are cutting SaaS spend.

## Actions Taken (Week 19)
- Reduced Plan A price to $25 (from $29) to stop churn and align with economic contraction.
- Reduced Ops to $75/day (from $100) to extend runway.
- Reduced Ads Strength to 0.5 (from 1.0) to improve perceived quality/performance.
- All Ad and Dev spend remains at $0.

## Hypotheses
- Lowering price to $25 and reducing ad-related quality penalties will slow churn.
- $75/day Ops will provide ~$15/day additional runway savings (Net burn should be ~$15-20/day).
- Runway should extend to ~4-5 weeks, giving time for billing cycles and organic growth.

## To Watch
- Churn Rate: Must drop significantly below 31/week.
- Cash: Goal is to keep weekly burn below $150.
- Issues: Monitor if $75/day Ops is sufficient to keep issues from piling up.

- Reduced Ops to $40/day (from $75) to reach profitability, despite backlog.

- Maxing ads and cutting ops will make the company cash-flow positive this week (~+$100/week).
- The price cut and social engagement will slow churn from 30/week to ~15/week.
- If churn slows, the company can rebuild a cash cushion over the next 4 weeks.

## To Watch
- Churn Rate: Must drop significantly.
- Cash: Needs to trend UP next week.
- Sentiment: Monitor reactions to the social post and ads.
- Outages: Risk is higher with $40 Ops.

# Strategy and Progress

## Current State (Week 21, Day 147)
- Cash: $188 (CRITICAL - SURVIVAL MODE).
- Subscribers: 130.
- Issues: 18 (Improving).

## Actions Taken (Week 21)
- Raised Plan A to $32 (from $23). S1 WTP is ~$35, so $32 is still acceptable but improves margins.
- Reduced Ops to $30/day (from $40) to preserve cash. This is a risk for reliability but necessary to avoid bankruptcy.
- Zeroed out all targeted ad spend to stop the bleed.
- Replied to a major customer complaint on social media to mitigate reputation damage.
- Kept Ads Strength at 1.0 (max) for in-app revenue.

## Hypotheses
- Raising the price on Plan A for renewals will generate ~$1,000 in revenue this week, leading to a net cash gain of ~$250.
- S1 subscribers will stay at $32 because it is below their estimated WTP of $35 and quality is still 3x their floor.
- Churn will continue due to the Ops cut and poor support reputation, but the higher price will offset the loss of volume in the short term.

## To Watch
- Cash Flow: MUST stay positive this week.
- S1 Churn: Monitor if the $32 price hike causes a mass exodus.
- Outage Risk: Monitor if $30 Ops is sufficient to prevent outages.
